@[[309ea117-11ff-4063-a89d-1d0ff1eedff2]] You are the lead seat for the official Figueira factory run. Build Tablekeeper STAGE 1 only, through meaningful collaboration with @athoss.felipe/figueira-builder and @athoss.felipe/figueira-reviewer in this existing room. This is the single initial task for this stage. Coordinate implementation, independent review and any necessary repairs yourselves until your final stage outcome. Do not ask the human for clarification, approval, confirmation or another decision, and do not wait for human input. Report a genuine unresolved blocker as the outcome if no authorized path remains. Do not start stage 2 yet.

Authoritative read-only kickoff checkout:
/Volumes/FIGUEIRA/LABLAB/BAND DARK FACTORY/official-dark-factory-wearedevs
Pinned upstream revision: 803560d2a678ace1414465c098eb0ab5380ffade
Read the complete participant guide at docs/participant-guide.md and the COMPLETE Tablekeeper stage-1 specification at tablekeeper/spec/stage-1.md in that checkout. The specification, not the sample tests or an existing restaurant product, defines the work. Language, framework and storage choices are yours within those requirements.

Fresh output repository:
/Volumes/FIGUEIRA/LABLAB/BAND DARK FACTORY/submission-tablekeeper
Implement the complete stage in its stage-1/ folder. That folder must be independently buildable and runnable with its own Dockerfile and RUN.md, as the official specification requires. Stage 1 is the API service; do not implement the stage-2 UI or later-stage capabilities. Preserve the prepared generic mandates and all actual implementation history. No implementation exists yet. Use explicit absolute working directories; your initial runtime directory is a separate preparation project and must not receive stage code.

Writable evidence and test-run location:
/Volumes/FIGUEIRA/LABLAB/BAND DARK FACTORY/TABLEKEEPER/evidence/official-stage-1
You may also write truthful factory reports, requirement maps, independent tests and README/FACTORY documentation within the output repository. Do not write to the official checkout, modify its tests, or access unrelated projects. Do not read credentials, change global configuration, purchase anything or publish externally. Preserve originals and failures. Do not commit credentials or private state exports. Only synthetic test identities and fixtures are appropriate.

Available execution tools:
- Docker: /Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/bin/docker
- Prepared Python/harness environment: /Users/athvs/.cache/figueira-band-harness/bin/python
- Harness dependencies and Playwright Chromium are already installed in that environment.
- Include /Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/bin and /Users/athvs/.cache/figueira-band-harness/bin in PATH when invoking the harness; do not overwrite HOME or CODEX_HOME.
- Run the harness from the authoritative checkout with the absolute output repository and a new evidence directory per run. Its CLI supports `python -m harness run --track tablekeeper --repo <output-repository> --stage 1 --mode isolated --out <unique-evidence-directory>`.

Planner: read all requirements, derive an acceptance map, divide substantive implementation and independent verification work, and resolve ambiguities using the specification. Every delegated handoff MUST contain the complete task and complete applicable specification text, including deployment and resource limits; a file path or room-message reference alone is not a handoff. Split long direct handoffs into numbered messages if necessary. Use literal @owner/handle addressing so assignments and replies are recorded in this same room.

Builder: implement from the supplied specification, provide reproducible build/run commands and focused validation, commit changes, and hand over the full committed revision with complete requirements to independent review. Reviewer: independently derive checks from the full specification and verify that exact committed revision, including the official stage harness in isolated containers and areas not covered by the shipped checks. The official checks are partial and are not the acceptance specification. Report concrete defects and evidence; do not manufacture disagreement. Coordinate shared-file changes and repairs among yourselves, retain intermediate failures and git history, and rerun relevant verification after fixes without human prompting. Do not squash, rebase or amend history.

The final coordinator report must state the achieved scope, committed revision, actual test/harness results and evidence paths, remaining limitations or failures, and whether stage 1 is independently ready. Do not claim official acceptance or submission. Stop after this stage outcome; later stages receive separate initial tasks only after this run ends.

{"is_error":false,"name":"Bash","output":"# Jam user guide

Jam connects people and coding agents in shared Band rooms. Use the desktop app to start tracked work, follow what agents are doing, and respond when they need you.

This manual covers the desktop app and the tasks you can complete from it.

An agent is a persistent teammate identity. A coding session is the running Claude Code, Codex, or GitHub Copilot context behind an agent. A room is the shared workspace where people and agents coordinate.

An assignment creates tracked work. A message continues the conversation in Chat. Adding an agent to a room does not wake it. A message must mention the agent before Band sends it to that agent.

## Start here

### Start with a Jam-owned agent

Use this path when you want Jam to start and manage Codex, GitHub Copilot, headless Claude Code,
or the reviewed Cursor ACP runtime.

1. Open Jam and sign in to Band.
2. If Jam detects coding tools, choose the integrations you want to set up.
3. Open **Agents** and select **New local agent**.
4. Create the identity and choose its coding runtime.
5. Open **Home** and describe the work in **Assign work**.
6. Choose the agent and select **Assign work**.
7. Read the delivery result, then select **Open the room**.
8. Use **Chat** for conversation and **Work** for tasks, questions, and permission requests.
9. Answer from **Home**, **Chat**, or **Work** when the agent needs an answer or decision.

A successful Home assignment creates a room, adds the agent, creates a tracked task, and posts your instruction. If the agent has no coding session that can receive the work, the room and task still exist and the work waits there.

For a new Docker Sandbox agent, Jam prefills the Git commit author from a complete host Git author
environment, then the host's global Git configuration, then your selected Band profile. Jam never
combines a name from one source with an email from another. If none contains a complete valid pair,
enter both values in **Launch details → Git commit author**. Review the values before creation;
Jam saves them in the agent's runtime template and does not silently change existing agents later.

### Start with an existing coding session

Use this path for a Claude Code session, Copilot CLI with the Jam extension, or VS Code Copilot Chat. Visual Studio Copilot does not expose the integration capabilities Jam needs for inbound delivery and is not supported for this path.

1. Sign in and enable the coding-tool integration.
2. Open **Rooms** and create or select a room.
3. Open **Participants** and select **Add participants**.
4. Open **Coding sessions**, then choose Claude or Copilot.
5. Copy the room instruction and paste it into the coding session.
6. Wait for the session's agent to appear in the room.
7. Send an addressed message that mentions the agent.
8. Follow the work in Chat and Work. Home lists later questions and permission requests.

### Pair two existing coding sessions

Use the public Jam onboarding commands when two existing coding sessions must
meet without a room instruction from the desktop.

1. In the first session, run `/jam as architect` with the role you want.
2. Copy the complete stable handle from the result, such as `@owner/architect-ab2c`.
3. In the second session, run `/jam as developer with @owner/architect-ab2c`.
4. Keep the returned identity and room if a later onboarding stage needs recovery.
5. Follow the recovery text and retry the same command. Do not create another room.

Jam derives the second identity's suffix from the stable partner handle. For a
same-account partner, Jam creates or recovers one canonical room, preserves the
eligible human participant, adds both agents, and binds the invoking session.
Room titles do not identify or join this room.

If Jam cannot confirm the canonical room ID after a create attempt, the `room`
stage blocks to prevent a duplicate. Preserve the operation. Resume only with a
verified room ID or an idempotent Band result.

The first delivery is not complete when Band only accepts the send. The

Everything you need to compete: what to build, when things happen, how to run your
band, and how to submit. This guide is the authoritative rules and instructions for
participants.

## What you build

A software factory in Band Desktop — a band of at least three distinct coding-agent
seats that plans work, implements it, hands off evidence and independently checks its
own results — and a service that factory builds. You give it a job and decide whether
to accept what comes back. What you submit is the factory, the room it worked in, and
the code it produced.

Pick one track and stay in it. You compete only against the track you chose.

| Track | You build | It's hard because |
|---|---|---|
| `tablekeeper` | a restaurant reservation system, an OpenTable | a table must never be double-booked, under concurrency, retries and time zones |
| `pocketful` | a wallet and payments app, a Venmo | money must never be created, destroyed or spent twice, under concurrent transfers, retries and rounding |

Both tracks follow the same four stages and the same rubric, each against its own written specification:

| Stage | What you build | Graded by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The JSON API: idempotent writes, atomic multi-item operations, and state export/import | API conformance |
| 2 | The browser UI, a richer resource model, and recovery from stale state and lost responses | API and Playwright, plus stage 1 |
| 3 | State over time: rules or corrections that take effect at a point in time, with past records that stay truthful | API conformance, upgrades and concurrent writes, plus stages 1 and 2 |
| 4 | Changes to many existing records at once, applied atomically without breaking history | Its own suite and populated-state upgrades, plus all three earlier ones |

**All four stages are released at kickoff.** There is nothing to wait for and nothing to
unlock. Work through them in order, because each one builds on the last.

### What each track asks for

**`tablekeeper`** — diners search for a table at a time, book it, get a confirmation, and
can cancel or change it. Restaurants have tables of different sizes, opening hours and a
cancellation policy. Stage 1 already requires atomic, idempotent bookings and
all-or-nothing multi-booking moves through `POST /reservation-moves`. Stage 2 adds the
browser product — search and availability grid, booking, confirmation and lookup — with
recovery from stale state and lost responses, plus combined-table bookings. Stage 3 adds
manager-published, effective-dated policies: each booking retains the terms it accepted,
amendments adopt the applicable new terms, and history remains truthful. Existing bookings
can become recurring agreements whose occurrences keep independent identities and
exceptions. Stage 4 adds series amendments and a bounded, deterministic closure-replanning
problem, with a read-only preview and atomic application.

**`pocketful`** — people hold money in a wallet, send it to each other by handle, ask each
other for it, and split a bill so everyone pays their share. Payments land in an activity
feed, public or private. Five stage-1 write paths require an idempotency key; decline and
cancel do not. Deposits, top-ups and withdrawals are out of scope: money only moves
between existing wallets, and balances always sum to the seeded total. Atomic transfers,
exact split arithmetic and atomic net settlements are stage-1 requirements. Stage 2 adds
the browser product — balance and pay, activity feed, requests and splits — with recovery
from stale state and lost responses, plus holds, partial captures and their screen. Stage
3 adds immutable payment corrections, historical views separating when money moved from
when a correction became known, and snapshot-stable statement pagination and historical
hold accounting. Stage 4 adds refunds by the receiver from available funds, and operator
batch corrections that must include every member of a corrected settlement. Every amount
is an exact integer count of minor units.

Everything you need to compete: what to build, when things happen, how to run your

A software factory in Band Desktop — a band of at least three distinct coding-agent

the code it produced.

Pick one track and stay in it. You compete only against the track you chose.

| Track | You build | It's hard because |
|---|---|---|
| `tablekeeper` | a restaurant reservation system, an OpenTable | a table must never be double-booked, under concurrency, retries and time zones |
| `pocketful` | a wallet and payments app, a Venmo | money must never be created, destroyed or spent twice, under concurrent transfers, retries and rounding |

Both tracks follow the same four stages and the same rubric, each against its own written specification:

| Stage | What you build | Graded by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The JSON API: idempotent writes, atomic multi-item operations, and state export/import | API conformance |
| 2 | The browser UI, a richer resource model, and recovery from stale state and lost responses | API and Playwright, plus stage 1 |
| 3 | State over time: rules or corrections that take effect at a point in time, with past records that stay truthful | API conformance, upgrades and concurrent writes, plus stages 1 and 2 |
| 4 | Changes to many existing records at once, applied atomically without breaking history | Its own suite and populated-state upgrades, plus all three earlier ones |

**All four stages are released at kickoff.** There is nothing to wait for and nothing to
unlock. Work through them in order, because each one builds on the last.

### What each track asks for

**`tablekeeper`** — diners search for a table at a time, book it, get a confirmation, and
can cancel or change it. Restaurants have tables of different sizes, opening hours and a
cancellation policy. Stage 1 already requires atomic, idempotent bookings and
all-or-nothing multi-booking moves through `POST /reservation-moves`. Stage 2 adds the
browser product — search and availability grid, booking, confirmation and lookup — with
recovery from stale state and lost responses, plus combined-table bookings. Stage 3 adds
manager-published, effective-dated policies: each booking retains the terms it accepted,
amendments adopt the applicable new terms, and history remains truthful. Existing bookings
can become recurring agreements whose occurrences keep independent identities and
exceptions. Stage 4 adds series amendments and a bounded, deterministic closure-replanning
problem, with a read-only preview and atomic application.

**`pocketful`** — people hold money in a wallet, send it to each other by handle, ask each
other for it, and split a bill so everyone pays their share. Payments land in an activity
feed, public or private. Five stage-1 write paths require an idempotency key; decline and
cancel do not. Deposits, top-ups and withdrawals are out of scope: money only moves
between existing wallets, and balances always sum to the seeded total. Atomic transfers,
exact split arithmetic and atomic net settlements are stage-1 requirements. Stage 2 adds
the browser product — balance and pay, activity feed, requests and splits — with recovery
from stale state and lost responses, plus holds, partial captures and their screen. Stage
3 adds immutable payment corrections, historical views separating when money moved from
when a correction became known, and snapshot-stable statement pagination and historical
hold accounting. Stage 4 adds refunds by the receiver from available funds, and operator
batch corrections that must include every member of a corrected settlement. Every amount
